To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the level of inter‐link consistency was found to be low, and (ii), in the absence of a measure of the level of consistency of the links that were created by the searchers in our experiments, it was not possible to determine whether the levels of search effectiveness that were obtained were related to levels of inter‐searcher consistency.

(1) the levels of consistency between sets of links created by different people for a given document are low, and (2) the levels of retrieval effectiveness obtained from the hypertext databases in which the links were inserted are low.
(i) the level of consistency between link‐sets is low; and (ii) there is no clear correlation between the level of consistency and the level of retrieval effectiveness.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a hypertext system for the retrieval of full‐text scientific documents.
the retrieval of objects from hypertext databases.
the retrieval effectiveness of hypertext databases, with the creation of links in such databases, and with the relationship between these two topics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in our study, there is no evidence of a relationship between the level of consistency and the level of effectiveness of searches carried out using hypertext databases.

, although the linkers were not able to agree on the links to be inserted between the paragraphs of a document, their inability to agree did not appear to be a major cause of a lack of effectiveness in the searches carried out on the hypertext databases.

the relationship between the level of consistency among linkers and the effectiveness of the search process is not clear and needs further investigation, although it is possible to draw a number of tentative conclusions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hypertext links are not as effective as index terms.
hypertext databases are not yet ready for use in real‐world situations.
hypertext is not a magic wand that will transform retrieval effectiveness.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is important to consider how the creation of hypelinks is carried out in a hypertext database, as this can have an impact on the effectiveness of searches.
the creation of hypotext links by humans can be a very time‐consuming and expensive process, and that the resulting links can be inconsistent and unreliable.

there is little relationship between the levels of consistency among the sets of hypertext links created by different people and the levels of effectiveness obtained in a set of searches in a hypertext database.
